title: Get Outta Here and Go On Home, and who first played Tiger Rag
summary: The closing number of a dance, its link to Tiger Rag, and a discussion of who featured Tiger Rag first.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: After the dance, we used to play a piece called Get Outta Here. Da-da-da. Da-da-da. Da-da-da. Da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. Get outta here. And gone home. See, the Lory went to work. What did he make out of that? What do you call it now? He does it.
They use it, they use it. But that's the first record I made with you, you remember? Yeah, that's what we recorded. Yeah, that was on the...

Get Outta Here and Go On Home. That's what they played. That's the last number. That's the last number you played, yeah. To tell the people that the dance was over, huh? Yeah. Get Outta Here and Go On Home. Did both of them play that tune? Who? All of them played. Every band played that, huh? All of them played that. Get Outta Here and Go On Home. Yeah. Well, some people think that Get Outta Here and Go On Home is the same tune as Tiger Rag. Is that true? No. It sounds like, uh, you know, you know...
There may be some parts of it, eh, you understand. Some parts of sound, like it.
Now, who do you think played Tiger Rag first? No.
I think, uh, who did really feature that Tiger Rag really was that Dixieland band.

Red. Yeah. But do you think that... Some people think that Jack Carey, you know, it was called Play Jack Carey or something, huh? You see, I think all Red Nichols is... I think all that thing come out.
